blogs.title: Bits vs Bytes – The Dawn Of One‑Bit Language Models
blogs.description: This post explains why shrinking every weight in transformer models down to just three tiny symbols (- 1 / 0 / + 1) lets large language models run faster, use less energy and stay competitive—with concrete numbers showing how BitNet b¹·⁵⁸ matches full‑precision models while cutting GPU memory usage nearly threefold.

blogs.title: Ternary Transformers – Inside the Architecture Of BitNet b¹·⁵⁸
blogs.description: Discover how standard matrix multiplications get rewired into pure integer math via ‘BitLinear’ layers, how weights are forced into {- 1, 0,+ 1} using an absmean rounding trick, why eight‑bit activations suffice across all layers—and why these changes allow researchers to train large models from scratch without losing accuracy.

blogs.title: Speed & Savings Unleashed – One‑Bit Models Beat Full Precision
blogs.description: See concrete numbers where BitNet b¹·⁵⁸ catches up to FP16 LLaMA starting at just three billion parameters yet runs up to four times faster while eating less than a third of GPU memory—even enabling seventy‐billion parameter models that slash latency and joule consumption by far.

blogs.title: Designing Chips That Speak One Bill – Why AI Drivers Are Turning Toward Ultra Tiny Arithmetic
blogs.description: This article maps out what silicon would look like for one‑bit language models—how pure integer adders replace floating‑point multipliers , what memory levers vanish thanks to ternary weights , how custom chips could cut energy per token beyond GPUs today , and why firms such as Groq are already prototyping dedicated LPUs.

blogs.title: Tiny Bits Big Impact – From Mobile Edge Devices To Long Contexts
blogs.description: Looking ahead at possibilities opened by dramatic memory drops in one‑bit networks—how a small model can fit cleanly into phone RAM or embedded CPU caches , enable twice‐as‐long interaction contexts thanks to halved KV caches , fit Mixture-of-Experts entirely on one chip , making truly large‐scale language intelligence possible everywhere.
